title: Hosted API Demo - Chat/Text Basics - Aegis Finance
summary: Introductory hosted API demo covering chat/text generation basics: streaming, key request params, retry behavior, and quick notes on latency/cost tradeoffs and security. Customer is evaluating for a customer support summarization & routing POC. AE + SE present; next steps include sending pricing, security docs, and a trial account for a 2-week POC.

Priya to share streaming best-practices doc and example code - due 2026-03-05
Customer to provision test prompts and sample documents for POC - internal by 2026-03-08
Schedule POC kickoff (30 min) - target week of 2026-03-09

Priya Shah - Share streaming examples + retries guide - 2026-03-05
John Reynolds - Provide sample data and success criteria - 2026-03-08
transcript: [00:00] Alex Carter: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, with me is Priya and Diego from SE - hey team

[00:08] John Reynolds: Hey Alex, thanks, John here. We have Maria, Samir and Ellie on, we're excited to see the hosted API. Quick context we run customer support routing and want to add summarization + triage via LLMs.

[00:18] Alex Carter: Awesome, that's helpful. Today we'll walk through the hosted API for chat and text gen, hit streaming, params like temperature and max tokens, and cover retry behavior - and leave time for Q&A.

[00:28] Priya Shah: Quick agenda slide - i'll share my screen  -  i'll share my screen - (link to deck) - demo will be live code + console tour. Note, transcription may be a bit rough, apologies if names are clipped.

[00:42] [00:42] Diego Morales: Jumping in  -  first slide is the simple request pattern. It's a single REST call or SDK call, you can stream tokens back so you get lower TTFB for the first token which is helpful for chat UI.
[00:58] Ellie Park: streaming is key for us, we need sub-300ms first byte for snappy UI, what's realistic on hosted?

[01:06] Priya Shah: Good question  -  on hosted with our curated small-medium models, first byte often 150-350ms at typical prompt sizes; larger models and long context push that up. We tune batching and kernel selection behind the scenes.
[01:22] Samir Patel: Are there SLOs for TTFB on hosted? We have enterprise latency constraints.

[01:27] Alex Carter: Hosted doesn't have the same SLA as Dedicated but we publish performance profiles in the model catalog; for hard latency SLOs we usually recommend Dedicated GPU pools. We'll include that in the pricing doc.
[01:40] John Reynolds: And on cost, we worry about token spend for summarization, what's the typical unit cost?

[01:46] Priya Shah: Cost depends on model and compressing prompts. Our Optimize tooling suggests batching and prefix caching to reduce tokens; for POC we can recommend a cheaper variant for routing and use higher-quality model for final summarization.
[01:58] [01:58] Diego Morales: Now demo time - open the console: routes, usage, streaming toggle. I'll run a live example of chat completions with streaming enabled.

[02:12] [02:12] Priya Shah: Sample code (node/python) sending a streaming request. Note the client accepts partial chunks and you can render them immediately. Example shows using an idempotency key on retries.

[02:26] Alex Carter: Important: retries - use idempotency key for 'at-most-once' or 'at-least-once' semantics. We recommend idempotency when you might re-send after timeouts so you don't double-bill or duplicate actions.
[02:38] Maria Chen: Can you explain how retries interact with streaming? If the stream drops mid-response do you start over?

[02:45] Priya Shah: If a connection drops, typical pattern is to retry at the application layer. With idempotency key we can resume or request a full regenerate. There is not a byte-range resume; you either get the streamed complete response or re-run and dedupe by key.
[02:58] John Reynolds: Okay that makes sense. What's the recommended timeout/retry policy?

[03:03] Priya Shah: We suggest conservative client timeout around 30s for single-turn gen, but for longer outputs increase. Retries: exponential backoff with jitter, and avoid aggressive retries for 5xx from the model service; handle 429 with a backing-off and maybe fallback to smaller model.
[03:18] [03:18] Diego Morales: Also we have built-in fallback policies in routing  -  if primary model is at capacity we can route to a compatible model variant automatically.
[03:26] Ellie Park: About params - temperature/top_p etc - do you have guidance for deterministic summaries?

[03:31] Priya Shah: For deterministic summarization use lower temperature (0-0.2) and a narrower top_p, also set stop sequences if you have clear delimiting tokens. Use max_tokens to cap length, and you can use logprobs for debugging.
[03:43] Samir Patel: Is there request-level cost prediction? We need to estimate monthly spend for X tickets/day.
[03:49] Alex Carter: In the console we show per-route cost breakdown and token-level cost estimates. For POC we'll produce an estimate using your sample ticket volume.
[03:59] John Reynolds: Security  -  we are in finance so SOC2 + encryption and SSO are non-negotiable. How does hosted handle data residency and logs?

[04:07] Alex Carter: Hosted is SOC2 compliant and we encrypt data at rest and transit; for stricter requirements we offer Dedicated or Private deployments with customer-managed VPC and KMS. We also have audit logs and RBAC in the Console.
[04:20] Maria Chen: Do you retain prompts and responses for training or product improvement?

[04:24] Priya Shah: By default Redwood does not use customer data to improve models  -  we have options to opt-out; we'll share the data-retention and privacy docs. For audit we can keep logs with configurable retention.
[04:36] [04:36] Diego Morales: Demo request  -  i'm sending a chat request now (shows curl). Streaming chunks coming in... partial tokens, final chunk. You can see how client handles them.
[04:50] Ellie Park: Nice. The partials look clean, slight hesitation when model emits long tokens but that's normal.
[04:57] John Reynolds: Any tips to reduce latency for multi-turn conversations? We have long histories.

[05:03] Priya Shah: Use prefix caching for KV cache where repeated context is reused; also trim unnecessary history, use embeddings to fetch relevant snippets rather than full transcript. For long context we recommend using models with longer context windows or summarizing history.
[05:17] Samir Patel: For PII, can we mask before sending or use client-side scrubbers?

[05:21] Priya Shah: Absolutely, we recommend scrubbing sensitive fields client-side and we can also provide hooks for token-level redaction. For Private deployments you'd have full control over scrubbers in your environment.
[05:32] [05:32] Diego Morales: Switching to code: here's example Node stream handler with reconnect logic and idempotency key header. Note the pattern for dedupe on regenerates.
[05:46] [05:46] transcription error: Speaker maybe mislabelled  -  code snippet shows `X-Request-ID` but our client uses `Idempotency-Key` header.
[05:58] Alex Carter: Good catch  -  we'll include exact header names in the examples we send, sorry for the slip.
[06:04] Maria Chen: Do you support function/tool calling or structured outputs? We need deterministic extraction of intent and routing code.

[06:12] Priya Shah: Yes, the hosted API supports structured output via JSON schema enforcement and function calling style  -  we can return well-formed JSON with checks. That helps for downstream routing.
[06:24] John Reynolds: For the POC, our success metrics are: 1) 85% accurate routing, 2) avg summary length < 80 words, 3) < $0.03 per ticket  -  are those achievable?

[06:36] Alex Carter: Those are reasonable targets. We'll help size model choices: cheap model for routing, higher-quality for final summary, and Optimize will suggest quantization/ batching for cost-savings.
[06:48] Ellie Park: Any limits on streaming payload sizes or max_tokens?

[06:52] Priya Shah: There are model-specific max token limits; we enforce a request max. If you need longer contexts, we can use longer-context variants. We'll surface errors when over limit and suggest chunking.
[07:04] Samir Patel: Rate limits? We have bursts during business hours.

[07:08] Alex Carter: Hosted has tiered rate limits and per-account quotas. For bursts, Dedicated offers predictable throughput and autoscale. For hosted you can request quota increases and set up retry/backoff patterns for bursting.

[07:20] [07:20] Diego Morales: Quick note on observability  -  Console shows token breakdown, latency per request, per-route dashboards, and traces. You can instrument your service with our SDK to correlate user IDs.
[07:32] John Reynolds: That trace correlation is helpful for debugging. Do we need to send user ids to Redwood? Any PII issues?
[07:38] Priya Shah: You can send pseudo-ids; avoid sending raw PII. We can also enable token scrubbing and custom retention windows.
[07:46] Maria Chen: What about retries causing duplicated side-effects if a completion triggers an action in our system?

[07:52] Alex Carter: Use idempotency keys for side-effecting calls, and handle at-most-once semantics. For safety pipelines, have the LLM produce a deterministic output that your orchestrator validates before actioning.
[08:04] [08:04] Ellie Park: Do you have a sample POC plan?

[08:08] Priya Shah: Yes: Week 0 - kickoff and install API keys/test account. Week 1 - integrate routing model and run internal tests. Week 2 - evaluate summary quality and tune params. Deliverable: dashboard with metrics and cost estimate.
[08:20] John Reynolds: That timeline works. Budget approval needs to go through procurement; we may need a short commercial summary for procurement and security.
[08:27] Alex Carter: We'll include a commercial one-pager and security whitepaper. I'll also loop in our security contact if you want an intro call.
[08:36] Maria Chen: Great. A couple of small technical follow-ups: sample code in Python, streaming reconnect example, and a note on how to run local benchmarks against your hosted endpoints.
[08:45] Priya Shah: We'll include a simple benchmark harness you can run to measure latency/cost with your prompts; it will help pick model variants for the POC.

[08:56] Diego Morales: Demo wrap-up  -  running an end-to-end from prompt to summary and then a JSON extraction. You can see the model produce the summary in streaming chunks and then the final JSON with fields intent: and severity:.
[09:10] John Reynolds: How do you recommend handling partial stream cancellations when user navigates away?

[09:15] Priya Shah: Cancel the stream client-side and optionally send a cancel event to your orchestration; treat partials as non-committal until final event is received. For billing, partial responses may still consume tokens, so be mindful.
[09:26] [09:26] transcription noise: slight background echo from one participant  -  some words mis-transcribed, e.g., "redwood" as "read wood" in one snippet.
[09:36] Ellie Park: Are there built-in SDK helpers for batching multiple short messages into one call?
[09:41] Diego Morales: Yes, our SDKs provide batching utilities and the runtime performs continuous batching to improve throughput; Optimize suggests batching windows for best cost/latency tradeoffs.
[09:52] Samir Patel: For billing, do you have detailed token logs per request? We need to reconcile with our internal logs.
[09:58] Alex Carter: We provide token-level usage per request in the Console and via API exports for finance reconciliation.
[10:06] John Reynolds: OK \u2014 last question: can you guarantee not to use POC data for model training?
[10:11] Priya Shah: Yes \u2014 we'll sign the data usage clause and by default hosted will not use customer data for training unless opt-in; procurement will want that in contract.

[10:20] Alex Carter: Great \u2014 recap: we'll send pricing & Dedicated options, streaming/retries docs, benchmark harness, and security whitepaper. Customer to provide sample tickets and success criteria for POC.
[10:31] Maria Chen: Sounds good. Let's aim to start the POC the week of 2026-03-09.
[10:36] Alex Carter: Thanks everyone \u2014 we'll follow up with the materials and a calendar invite for the kickoff. Any other quick Qs?
[10:42] John Reynolds: None from me, thanks Alex/Priya/Diego.
[10:45] Ellie Park: Thanks all, bye.
[10:47] Alex Carter: Bye \u2014 talk soon.
